A SERMON OF THE PALE SEAT AND THE KEEPER OF STORES

Attend, ash-bearers. Stand beneath the cold light and listen, for
the coast does not soften its stones, and neither should the heart
soften its vigilance.

Fenthrone was founded in 229 AS upon the Pale Coast. Mark that year
in your memory—not as a comfort, but as a warning. A seat raised
beside the pallor of the sea is not raised for ease. Its walls face
outward. Its watch is unending. Its silence is the silence of a
drawn blade.

Fenthrone is garrisoned by 5,805 troops. Let no tongue call such a
number merely a number. Each count is a burden accepted. Each count
is a place kept from emptiness. Yet even with that host, Fenthrone
remains outside the realm's core holdings. There is a lesson for
those who dwell far from the center: the edge is not lesser because
the throne does not look upon it every hour. The edge is where ruin
first tests the door.

Look upon Fenthrone in the mind: a fortified coastal seat framed by
the stark pallor of the Pale Coast. Its stones are watchful. Its
discipline is permanent. Its breath is measured. It does not promise
safety; it promises readiness. And readiness, faithful ones, is a
harsher blessing than comfort. Comfort teaches the soul to sleep.
Readiness teaches it to remain standing while the dark gathers
beyond the walls.

Now hear the name of Ossric Ashgrove.

He is a minor figure of the Ashen Era, and his birth was in 333 AS.
He serves as a quartermaster. Do not despise the keeper of stores
because his work is counted in ledgers, bundles, rations, tools, and
sealed rooms. The spear may glitter before the eye, but the spear is
not fed by glory. Armies endure by what is measured, preserved, and
placed into waiting hands.

No canonical physical details are recorded of Ossric Ashgrove. Let
this absence rebuke us. We hunger to carve every servant into stone,
to give every laborer a face fit for remembrance. Yet the work of a
quartermaster may be known without spectacle. His canonical
temperament is unrecorded. Therefore judge not the silence. The
silent page is not permission for invention.

Fenthrone keeps watch upon the Pale Coast. Ossric Ashgrove keeps the
work of supply. One stands beyond the core; the other stands behind
the line. Both remind us that endurance is built from duties
accepted without applause.

So go forth: be wall where a wall is needed, measure where measure
is needed, and let no neglected place become an open gate.
